rationale: SGLT2 reabsorbs filtered glucose in proximal tubule; inhibition causes glucosuria + osmotic natriuresis/volume contraction. Human LoF (familial renal glucosuria) is benign with no exercise/cardiac phenotype. SGLT2i reduce MACE/HF-hospitalisation (EMPA-REG/DECLARE/EMPEROR) = a validated cardiometabolic event-reduction axis.
H+/K+-ATPase alpha subunit = the gastric proton pump; sole role is parietal-cell acid secretion.
H+/K+-ATPase beta subunit; gastric acid secretion.
Mitochondrial complex I subunit; metformin partial inhibition raises AMP/ATP -> AMPK.
AMPK beta1; energy-sensing, suppresses hepatic gluconeogenesis.
Adenosine A1 receptor; caffeine antagonism -> wakefulness, vasoconstriction.
Adenosine A2A receptor; arousal, vasodilation.
Adenosine A2B; vascular/inflammatory.
Adenosine A3.
Androgen receptor; anabolic on muscle MASS (hypertrophy), distinct from oxidative/aerobic capacity.
Nintedanib blocks FGFR -> antifibrotic (fibroblast proliferation) + antiangiogenic.
PDGFR drives fibroblast proliferation/myofibroblast activation; core antifibrotic axis.
VEGFR2; antiangiogenic + contributes to antifibrotic effect.
Vasopressin V2 receptor; sets urine concentration AND drives cyst-epithelial cAMP -> the validated rate-limiting driver of ADPKD cyst growth (tolvaptan).
Angiotensin-II type-1 receptor; modulates renal plasma flow / efferent arteriolar tone and systemic vascular tone.
Lubiprostone activates intestinal apical Cl- secretion (ClC-2/CFTR) -> luminal fluid -> motility.
Alpha-1A adrenoceptor dominates bladder-neck/prostatic smooth muscle tone; blockade relieves outlet obstruction.
Alpha-1D adrenoceptor; bladder/detrusor and vascular tone.
VMAT2 loads monoamines into synaptic vesicles; inhibition depletes presynaptic dopamine release (treats hyperkinetic movement), NOT postsynaptic D2 psychosis signalling.
Mineralocorticoid receptor; Na/water retention, cardiac/renal remodelling.
NK3 receptor (KNDy neurons) directly drives hypothalamic thermoregulatory vasomotor flushes.
M3 muscarinic receptor mediates airway (and detrusor) smooth-muscle contraction; antagonists (LAMA) bronchodilate -> FEV1.
M1 muscarinic; contributes to cholinergic airway tone (anticholinergic bronchodilation).
Beta-2 adrenoceptor mediates airway smooth-muscle relaxation; agonists (SABA/LABA) bronchodilate -> FEV1.
Glucocorticoid receptor; inhaled/systemic corticosteroids suppress airway and systemic inflammation.
CFTR chloride channel; modulators (ivacaftor/lumacaftor) restore airway-surface ion/fluid transport -> CF FEV1.
Endothelin-A receptor drives pulmonary (and systemic) vasoconstriction; antagonists (bosentan/macitentan/ambrisentan) lower PVR in PAH.
Endothelin-B receptor; dual ERAs lower pulmonary vascular tone in PAH.
PDE5 inhibition (sildenafil/tadalafil) raises cGMP -> pulmonary vasodilation in PAH.
Prostacyclin (IP) receptor agonists (selexipag/epoprostenol) cause pulmonary vasodilation in PAH.
Soluble guanylate cyclase (riociguat) -> cGMP -> pulmonary vasodilation in PAH/CTEPH.
Beta-1 adrenoceptor; beta-blockade reduces contractility/rate; beta-agonism (dobutamine) raises cardiac output/perfusion. NOT an airway lever.
HMG-CoA reductase; statins lower cholesterol synthesis and reduce MACE (4S/CARE/JUPITER) = a validated atherothrombotic event-reduction axis. Not an airway or anti-exacerbation lever.
Vitamin D receptor; calcium/immune modulation. Not an established airway-exacerbation lever.

PDE3 inhibition (milrinone) is a positive inotrope/pulmonary vasodilator; in platelets PDE3 inhibition (cilostazol) raises cAMP -> antiplatelet + vasodilation, a validated secondary-stroke/PAD event-reduction axis (CSPS2).
Mu-opioid receptor; agonists directly suppress ascending nociceptive transmission.
Kappa-opioid receptor; analgesic via nociceptive modulation.
COX-2 makes prostaglandins that sensitise nociceptors; NSAID/coxib inhibition is analgesic (esp. inflammatory pain).
COX-1; prostaglandin-mediated nociceptor sensitisation.
Nav1.7 sensory sodium channel; gain-of-function causes pain, loss-of-function causes congenital insensitivity -> direct nociceptive lever.
Nav1.8 sensory sodium channel in nociceptors.
Nav1.9 sensory sodium channel in nociceptors.
Capsaicin receptor on nociceptors; thermal/inflammatory pain transduction.
P2X3 on sensory afferents; gefapixant target for chronic cough and sensory hypersensitivity.
CGRP receptor (with RAMP1); CGRP pathway drives migraine; antagonists/antibodies are antimigraine.
CGRP ligand; trigeminovascular migraine mediator.
5-HT3 receptor; setrons block the emetic reflex (CINV/PONV).
5-HT4 agonists (prucalopride) are prokinetic -> GI motility.
Guanylate cyclase-C agonists (linaclotide) raise cGMP -> intestinal fluid secretion.
Gastric H+/K+-ATPase; PPI target (duplicate-safe).
D2 receptor; antipsychotic (psychosis) AND antiemetic (area postrema) -> process depends on the endpoint.
Cardiac beta-myosin heavy chain; mavacamten directly reduces sarcomere hypercontractility -> lowers LVOT obstruction in HCM.
Cardiac alpha-myosin heavy chain; sarcomere contractility.
Vitamin-K epoxide reductase; warfarin anticoagulation -> dissolves/prevents LV thrombus and reduces cardioembolic stroke/VTE events.
Factor Xa; apixaban/rivaroxaban anticoagulation -> LV thrombus resolution; reduces cardioembolic stroke/VTE events.
Thrombin; anticoagulant target; reduces thromboembolic events.

ADP receptor on platelets; clopidogrel/ticagrelor antiplatelet -> reduces atherothrombotic events (CAPRIE/PLATO). A validated event-reduction axis (efficacy is indication-dependent: strong in ACS, weaker in acute stroke/PAD).
Platelet GP IIb subunit; GP IIb/IIIa antagonism (abciximab) inhibits final-common-path platelet aggregation -> atherothrombotic event reduction.
Platelet GP IIIa subunit; GP IIb/IIIa antagonism inhibits platelet aggregation -> atherothrombotic event reduction.
PCSK9 degrades LDL receptor; mAb inhibition lowers LDL and reduces MACE (FOURIER/ODYSSEY) = validated atherothrombotic event-reduction axis.
Intestinal cholesterol transporter; ezetimibe lowers LDL and reduces MACE on top of statin (IMPROVE-IT).
Apolipoprotein B; antisense (mipomersen) lowers LDL particle number, an atherogenic-lipid event-reduction axis.
GLP-1 receptor agonism (liraglutide/semaglutide) reduces MACE in diabetes/obesity (LEADER/SELECT) = validated cardiometabolic event-reduction axis.
Xanthine oxidase; allopurinol lowers urate (NOT a renal-hemodynamic lever).
Beta-3 adrenoceptor; mirabegron relaxes detrusor -> bladder capacity.
M2 muscarinic on detrusor; antimuscarinics (oxybutynin) increase bladder capacity.
Glucosylceramide synthase; venglustat reduces glycosphingolipids (a CONTRIBUTOR, not the validated rate-limiter of ADPKD cyst growth).
Prostaglandin F receptor; latanoprost increases uveoscleral outflow -> lowers IOP.
Carbonic anhydrase II; dorzolamide/brinzolamide reduce aqueous humour production -> lower IOP.
Alpha-2 agonists (brimonidine) reduce aqueous production -> lower IOP.
